div.p: A to-do list for Google. One row per ticket whose sheet entry is out of date, written in the same transaction as the ticket itself, so "the ticket exists" and "the sheet owes an update" become true together. The worker drains it; status moves PENDING → SENT, or → FAILED after five attempts.

It lives in Postgres rather than only in Redis for that reason: a Redis dispatch can be lost while the ticket commits, and nothing would ever know the sheet was stale. The Redis job is only a nudge — the outbox is the record.

p.strong: Why this runs out of band

div.p: Google Sheets is slow, rate limited (~60 writes/min/user), and owned by someone else. Inside the encoding request, every ticket save would inherit Google's latency and every Google outage would look like the system being down. The outbox buys separation: the ticket is safe the moment it commits, and the sheet catches up.
Batching matters most at backfill. The existing sheet history goes through this same path. One batched call per 100 rows stays under the rate limit; 100 individual calls will not.
raw_row_number is only ever a cache. If it is missing or stale, the worker falls back to locating the row by row_key. Correctness never depends on the cached index — that was the original bug.

g.text: Claim a batch of pending work
Project each ticket to a sheet row
sign JWT with service account key
